--- title: "Making Things: Is the Factory Humming?" date: "2026-01-19" categories: [news, data, economics] image: image.png format: html: code-fold: false jupyter: python3 --- ## The Hype The news wires were humming this week like a cicada in summer with reports that US Industrial Production ticked up by 0.4% in December. G'day folks! Dinki here. It all sounds decent, like finding a fresh patch of grass, but percentages without context are like a wombat without a burrow—exposed. Is this a real recovery or just a blip? Note: this is just a test post to make sure all the automated workflows are working as expected. ## The Dig We went straight to the source: the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED). We grabbed the **Industrial Production: Total Index (INDPRO)**. This index measures the real output of all relevant establishments located in the United States. **Data Source**: [FRED Industrial Production Index (INDPRO)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/INDPRO) ::: {#cell-analysis .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Load the data # The data is in the source_data directory relative to this post df = pd.read_csv("../../source_data/2026-01-19-industrial-production/INDPRO.csv") # Clean up dates df['DATE'] = pd.to_datetime(df['observation_date']) df = df.rename(columns={'INDPRO': 'Industrial_Production'}) # Let's filter to the last 10 years to see the modern context recent_df = df[df['DATE'] >= '2016-01-01'] # Show the raw numbers (transparency!) display(recent_df.tail()) ``` ::: {#analysis .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## What We Found When you look at the last decade, you can see the massive crater left by the 2020 lockdowns. Since then, we climbed back up, but we've been bouncing along a plateau for the last couple of years. The recent "0.4% increase" looks like a tiny wiggle on a very flat line. ::: {#cell-visualization .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6)) sns.lineplot(data=recent_df, x='DATE', y='Industrial_Production', linewidth=2.5, color='#2c3e50') plt.title('US Industrial Production (2016 - Present)', fontsize=16, fontweight='bold') plt.xlabel('Year', fontsize=12) plt.ylabel('Index (2017=100)', fontsize=12) plt.axhline(y=recent_df['Industrial_Production'].max(), color='r', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5, label='Peak') plt.legend() plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/visualization-output-1.png){#visualization width=1137 height=561} ::: ::: ## Conclusion The factories are running, but they aren't exactly sprinting. We are hovering near all-time highs, but unable to break out significantly above the levels we reached back in 2022. The 0.4% rise is positive, but in the grand scheme of things, it's just maintaining altitude. Hooroo for now! Data don't lie, but sometimes they mumble. Correct me on GitHub if I misheard.
